title: Haemodialysis principles and prescription

steps.tx: Extracorporeal solute clearance during modern hemodialysis operates via two distinct biophysical processes: **diffusion** and **convection**. Diffusion is driven by concentration gradients across semipermeable hollow-fiber membrane pores, whereas convection (**solute drag**) accompanies bulk fluid ultrafiltration driven and generated by transmembrane hydrostatic pressure gradients across dialyzers.

left.title: Diffusive Transport
points: Governed by Fick law and dialyzer KoA
Dependent on blood and dialysate flow rates

right.title: Convective Transport
points: Solutes dragged alongside bulk water flux

steps.tx: The dialyzer **mass transfer area coefficient** (**KoA**), expressed in mL/min, quantifies maximum clearance capacity for a solute at infinite blood and dialysate flow rates. High-efficiency modern dialyzers boast a urea KoA exceeding **600** to **800** mL/min, reflecting dense hollow-fiber packing and optimized countercurrent fluid dynamics.

left.title: Clinical Sequence
points: Dialyzer membrane surface area and pore size
KoA > 600 to 800 mL/min for small solutes

steps.tx: Contemporary synthetic **High-flux hemodialysis** membranes are classified by an ultrafiltration coefficient (**Kuf**) > **20** mL/h/mmHg and a **beta-2 microglobulin** clearance exceeding **20** mL/min. These biocompatible membranes provide superior clearance of middle molecular uremic toxins and inflammatory mediators compared to historical low-flux cellulose dialyzers.
steps.say: Contemporary synthetic High-flux hemodialysis membranes are classified by an ultrafiltration coefficient greater than 20 mL/h/mmHg and a beta-2 microglobulin clearance exceeding 20 mL/min. These biocompatible membranes provide superior clearance of middle molecular uremic toxins and inflammatory mediators compared to historical low-flux cellulose dialyzers.

steps.tx: Online **Hemodiafiltration** (**HDF**) combines high diffusive transport with high-volume convective fluid exchange exceeding **23** liters of substitution fluid per session in post-dilution mode. In the multicenter **CONVINCE** randomized trial, high-dose hemodiafiltration significantly reduced all-cause mortality compared with high-flux hemodialysis in chronic kidney failure.

steps.tx: International **KDOQI adequacy** guidelines mandate a minimum delivered single-pool **Kt/V** (**spKt/V**) of **1.2** per session (corresponding to a **urea reduction ratio** of **65%**) for patients undergoing thrice-weekly hemodialysis. Clinical prescription targets a delivered spKt/V of **1.4** (**70%** URR) to accommodate treatment interruptions.
steps.say: International KDOQI adequacy guidelines mandate a minimum delivered single-pool Kt/V of 1.2 per session, corresponding to a urea reduction ratio of 65%, for patients undergoing thrice-weekly hemodialysis. Clinical prescription targets a delivered single-pool Kt/V of 1.4 or 70% URR to accommodate treatment interruptions.

steps.tx: Standard **bicarbonate dialysate** formulas maintain sodium at **135** to **142** mmol/L, potassium at **2.0** to **3.0** mmol/L, ionized calcium at **1.25** to **1.50** mmol/L (or **2.5** to **3.0** mEq/L), magnesium at **0.5** mmol/L, and bicarbonate at **32** to **38** mmol/L to correct chronic metabolic acidosis.

right.title: Clinical Adjustments
points: Lower calcium for hypercalcemic adynamic bone
Isotonic sodium to prevent muscle cramps

steps.tx: Post-dialysis **Urea rebound** occurs **30** to **60** minutes following treatment completion due to multi-compartmental solute disequilibrium between intracellular and extracellular fluid volumes. This rebound phenomenon results in an **equilibrated Kt/V** (**eKt/V**) that is approximately **0.2** units lower than the uncorrected single-pool calculation.

nodes.label: Rapid intravascular urea clearance during dialysis
Delayed intracellular to extracellular urea diffusion
Equilibrated eKt/V is 0.2 units lower than spKt/V

steps.tx: Modern water treatment systems utilizing **reverse osmosis** must strictly conform to **ISO standards** for hemodialysis water quality. Conventional water requires viable **bacterial counts** < **100** CFU/mL and **endotoxin** < **0.25** EU/mL, whereas ultrapure water demands rigorous microbiological standards < **0.1** CFU/mL and < **0.03** EU/mL.
